questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a right-angled $\triangle ABC$, the measures of the angles are in an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) If its smallest side is $4$ units, then the area of $\triangle ABC$ is.....
questions.solution:
Let the angles of the right-angled triangle be $a - d$, $a$, and $a + d$.

The sum of the angles in a triangle is $180^{\circ}$.

$(a - d) + a + (a + d) = 180^{\circ} \Rightarrow 3a = 180^{\circ} \Rightarrow a = 60^{\circ}$

Since the triangle is right-angled, the largest angle is $90^{\circ}$.

$a + d = 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow 60^{\circ} + d = 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow d = 30^{\circ}$

The angles of the triangle are $30^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$, and $90^{\circ}$.

The smallest side is opposite to the smallest angle, which is $30^{\circ}$. Let this side be $x = 4$ units.

The other perpendicular side, opposite to $60^{\circ}$, is $y = x \tan 60^{\circ} = 4\sqrt{3}$ units.

The area of the right-angled triangle is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times x \times y$.

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 4\sqrt{3} = 8\sqrt{3}$ sq. units.

Answer: $8\sqrt{3}$ sq. units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n$ are in arithmetic progression with common difference d, then $\tan\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_1 a_2}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_2 a_3}\right) + \ldots + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_{n-1} a_n}\right)\right] = $ ____
questions.solution:
Given $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ are in arithmetic progression with common difference $d$.

$d = a_2 - a_1 = a_3 - a_2 = \ldots = a_n - a_{n-1}$

The general term of the series is:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_{k+1} - a_k}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right)$

Using the identity $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{1 + xy}\right) = \tan^{-1} x - \tan^{-1} y$, we get:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_{k+1} - a_k}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right) = \tan^{-1} a_{k+1} - \tan^{-1} a_k$

Let $S$ be the sum of the inverse trigonometric series:

$S = \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right)$

$S = (\tan^{-1} a_2 - \tan^{-1} a_1) + (\tan^{-1} a_3 - \tan^{-1} a_2) + \ldots + (\tan^{-1} a_n - \tan^{-1} a_{n-1})$

This is a telescoping sum, which simplifies to:

$S = \tan^{-1} a_n - \tan^{-1} a_1$

Applying the inverse tangent difference formula:

$S = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_n - a_1}{1 + a_1 a_n}\right)$

The given expression is $\tan(S)$:

$\tan(S) = \tan\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_n - a_1}{1 + a_1 a_n}\right)\right] = \dfrac{a_n - a_1}{1 + a_1 a_n}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{1}{6} \sin \theta, \cos \theta, \tan \theta$ are in G.P., then the general solution of $\theta$ is
questions.solution: Given the progression $a = \frac{1}{6} \sin \theta$, $b = \cos \theta$, $c = \tan \theta$ are in geometric progression, the condition holds: $b^2 = ac$. Substitute the expressions: $(\cos \theta)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{6} \sin \theta\right) (\tan \theta)$. Since $\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}$, \(\cos^2 \theta = \frac{1}{6} \sin \theta \cdot \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}.\) Multiplying both sides by $\cos \theta$ ($\cos \theta \neq 0$): \(\cos^3 \theta = \frac{1}{6} \sin^2 \theta.\) Using $\sin^2 \theta = 1 - \cos^2 \theta$: \(\cos^3 \theta = \frac{1}{6}(1 - \cos^2 \theta).\) Multiply by 6 and rearrange: \(6 \cos^3 \theta + \cos^2 \theta - 1 = 0.\) Let $x = \cos \theta$: \(6x^3 + x^2 - 1 = 0.\) Check rational roots: $x = \frac{1}{2}$ satisfies the equation, so it is a root. Factor the cubic: $(2x - 1)(3x^2 + 2x + 1) = 0$. The quadratic factor $3x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0$ has discriminant $D = 4 - 12 = -8 \lt 0$, so no real roots. Thus, $\cos \theta = \frac{1}{2}$, and the general solution is $\theta = 2n\pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3}$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. The answer matches option A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The money invested in a company is compounded continuously. ₹400 invested today becomes $₹ 800$ in 6 years, then at the end of 33 years, it will become _{-}(\sqrt{2} = 1 \cdot 4142)
questions.solution:
Continuous compounding follows the formula $A = Pe^{rt}$, where $P$ is the principal, $r$ the annual rate, and $t$ the time in years.

To find $r$, set $P = 400$, $A = 800$, and $t = 6$:
$800 = 400e^{6r}$
$2 = e^{6r}$
Taking natural logarithms: $\ln(2) = 6r$, so $r = \frac{\ln(2)}{6}$.

For $t = 33$ years, with the same $P$ and $r$:
$A = 400e^{\left(\frac{\ln(2)}{6}\right) \cdot 33} = 400e^{5.5\ln(2)} = 400e^{\ln(2^{5.5})} = 400 \cdot 2^{5.5}$

Since $2^{5.5} = 2^5 \cdot 2^{0.5} = 32\sqrt{2} \approx 32 \cdot 1.4142 = 45.2544$,
$A = 400 \cdot 45.2544 = 18101.76$

This matches option B.

questions.solution:
$\sin (\theta-\alpha), \sin \theta$ and $\sin (\theta+\alpha)$ are in H.P. $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sin (\theta-\alpha)}, \frac{1}{\sin \theta}, \frac{1}{\sin (\theta+\alpha)}$ will be in A.P.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad & \frac{2}{\sin \theta}=\frac{1}{\sin (\theta-\alpha)}+\frac{1}{\sin (\theta+\alpha)} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2}{\sin \theta}=\frac{\sin (\theta+\alpha)+\sin (\theta-\alpha)}{\sin (\theta-\alpha) \sin (\theta+\alpha)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{2}{\sin \theta}=\frac{2 \sin \theta \cos \alpha}{\sin ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \alpha} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \alpha=\sin ^2 \theta \cos \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta(1-\cos \alpha)=\sin ^2 \alpha\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta\left(2 \sin ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2}\right)=4 \sin ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 1-\cos ^2 \theta=2 \cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta=1-2 \cos ^2 \frac{\alpha}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A radioactive substance, with initial mass $m_0$, has a half-life of $\mathrm{h}$ days. Then its initial decay rate is given by

$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\mathrm{km} \text {, where } \mathrm{k}\gt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{m}}=-\mathrm{kdt}\end{aligned}$
Integrating on both sides, we get
$\log m=-k t+c$
When $\mathrm{t}=0, \mathrm{~m}=\mathrm{m}_0\therefore \quad \log \mathrm{m}_0=0+\mathrm{c}\Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\log \mathrm{m}_0\therefore \quad \log m=-k t+\log m_0\Rightarrow \log \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{m}_0}=-\mathrm{kt}$
When $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{m}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}_0\therefore \quad \log \left(\frac{\frac{1}{2} m_0}{m_0}\right)=-k h\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \log \frac{1}{2}=-\mathrm{kh} \\ & \Rightarrow \log 2=\mathrm{kh}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=\frac{\log 2}{\mathrm{~h}}$  ...(i)

questions.q: Rate of increase of bacteria in a culture is proportional to the number of bacteria present at that instant and it is found that the number doubles in 6 hours. The number of bacteria becomes times at the end of 18 hours.
questions.solution:
Let $P_0$ be the initial population and let the population after $t$ years be $P$. Then,

\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{dP}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{kP} \text {, where } \mathrm{k}>0 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dP}}{\mathrm{P}}=\mathrm{kdt}
\end{aligned}

Integrating on both sides, we get

\begin{aligned}
& \log \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{kt}+\mathrm{c} \\
& \text { When } \mathrm{t}=0, \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{P}_0 \\
& \therefore \quad \log \mathrm{P}_0=0+\mathrm{c} \\
& \Rightarrow c=\log \mathrm{P}_0 \\
& \log \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{kt}+\log \mathrm{P}_0 \\
& \Rightarrow \log \frac{\mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{P}_0}=\mathrm{kt} \\
& \begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & \log \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{kt}+\log \mathrm{P}_0 \\
& \Rightarrow \log \frac{\mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{P}_0}=\mathrm{kt} \\
& \text { When } \mathrm{t}=6 \text { hrs, } \mathrm{P}=2 \mathrm{P}_0
\end{aligned} \\
& \therefore \quad \log \frac{2 \mathrm{P}_0}{\mathrm{P}_0}=6 \mathrm{k} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=\frac{\log 2}{6} \\
& \therefore \quad \log \frac{P}{P_0}=\frac{\log 2}{6} t \\
& \text { When } \mathrm{t}=18 \mathrm{hrs} \text {, we have } \\
& \log \frac{P}{P_0}=\frac{\log 2}{6} \times 18 \\
& =3 \log 2 \\
& \therefore \quad \log \frac{P}{P_0}=\log 8 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}=8 \mathrm{P}_0 \\
&
\end{aligned}
